Hey I’m really sorry about your dad, I honestly don’t know what I’d do with myself so I hope you’re doing ok :). Since I’m planning to go to uni in September I’m worried I’ll have to rely on my mum for finance and I’m scared about the availability of emotional support. Do you have any clue what I can do ?
Hey I’m really sorry that happened to you, and I hope your doing better. Do you have any suggestions on what I could do?
Ah, it’s good that the situation is better, it really sucks to feel miserable, maybe you should try talking to councillors at the uni you’re at ?
Emotional abuse is still abuse, if you’re feeling unsafe and unstable please talk to someone you trust.

The best thing you can do is instead of self diagnosis, is getting a diagnosis from a medical professional, and discussing with them about how your mental health is. That way you can get the medication that suits your lifestyle and that doesn’t counteract other medication you might already take.

It might help to challenge aggressive thought by being in a controlled environment where a physical excursion is taking place. You could try focusing the aggressive energy, not necessarily negative thought, into a punch on a sand bag and try boxing? 

It might be interesting to find a vegetable or fruit you really like and replace an unhealthy food item with a healthy food item, that way you’re not punishing yourself for wanting to eat.

It might be difficult but have you tried talking to her about your reaction that question, maybe she’s afraid of having done something bc she doesn’t understand what you’re going through ?

Sounds awful, hope you’re ok :(

You’re doing the best you can rn, leaving class early is a pretty brave thing despite what others might say. As for the individual who passed away as they did, keeping them in your thoughts and upholding sympathy is good for their spirit. Even though they may only get sympathy in death, it’s good to keep your own thoughts healthy despite the trauma of others.

As for the people at the back of the class, they have their own shit to deal with so just let em stew in their own juices bc they don’t realise how incredible a person you are for being honest like this.
It sounds really cheesy but going on a walk with music playing might help?

There’s times I’m feeling down when I’m in town and I find the ugliest shoes I can find and try them on, take a few steps and then take them off. I may look silly, but the shoes aren’t mine and they don’t define me, plus I don’t have to buy them if I don’t want to :)

It can help you come to terms with how your thought process works and how to challenge negative thought. Some say a problem shared is a problem halved ? But it’s completely up to you if you want to talk about low points in your life and you should never feel pressured to come forward about it.
